name: Dexterity Mech
summary: A dual-arm industrial mobile manipulator on a four-wheel-steer rover for truck loading, unloading and palletizing, with a 5.4 m arm span, 60 kg lift and over 2.4 m vertical reach. FedEx uses it for trailer loading at its Hagerstown hub.

germany.statusNote: No German or EU sales route found; Dexterity (Redwood City, California) sells through contact@dexterity.ai and designs and assembles Mech in California.

specs.label: Lift capacity
specs.quote: With two arms, it achieves a 5.4m armspan and can lift 60kg.

specs.label: Arm span
specs.quote: With two arms, it achieves a 5.4m armspan and can lift 60kg.

specs.label: Vertical reach
specs.quote: Mech's vertical reach safely extends beyond 2.4 meters

specs.label: Operating conditions
specs.value: 0 to 50 °C, up to 1,500 m altitude, up to 90% humidity
specs.quote: built to operate in 0°-50°C temperatures, up to 1,500m altitude, and up to 90% humidity

specs.label: Arm hardware
specs.value: Two arms made by Kawasaki, motion components by HIWIN; 4 kHz torque control
specs.quote: Mech's arms are manufactured by Kawasaki

specs.label: Rover base
specs.value: Four steerable wheels, strafes and climbs ramps; dual vacuum pumps, up to 16 cameras
specs.quote: Mech's rover base moves, spins, strafes, and climbs ramps, with all four wheels steerable.

specs.label: Software
specs.value: 68+ autonomous skill agents (Dexterity Physical AI, Foresight world model)
specs.quote: Every Mech runs Dexterity's Physical AI - a fleet of 68+ autonomous skill agents

notes: Picks boxes, parcels and polybags with vacuum grippers (dual vacuum pumps on the rover).
Arm payload is the combined two-arm lift (60 kg).
The maker calls it an "industrial superhumanoid" but stresses it is not a humanoid: wheeled rover with two industrial arms.
